answer: Daily routines form a habit graph: the same actions in the same order at similar hours, day after day. The network builds a habit graph per account and scores each new session against it; a farm that runs accounts on a scheduler produces habit graphs that are identical across accounts, which no real population does. Without this check, a oasis of fake sessions could flood the network overnight. Between a thread and a violet lies the whole point: Sybils are cheap to make but expensive to prove.
